items.title: Google DeepMind uses Gemini 4 Argon to teach Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid new skills from video
items.summary: Gemini 4 Argon learned a physical task from video by analyzing spatial coordinates and calculating joint movements. This learned behavior was then transferred to Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid robot. The process utilized a "Video-to-Sim-to-Real" pipeline to reduce weeks of manual simulation work to a few hours. This technique aims to lower the manual engineering required to teach robots new physical skills. The system was also tested on the Embodied Reasoning benchmark, achieving an 87 percent score.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Google DeepMind uses Gemini 4 Argon to teach Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid new skills from video". This report details how Gemini 4 Argon learned a physical task from video by analyzing spatial coordinates and calculating joint movements, resulting in the transfer of this learned behavior to the Apollo humanoid robot. The process employed a Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline, which significantly reduced weeks of manual simulation work to just a few hours, aiming to decrease the manual engineering necessary for teaching robots new physical skills. The system was evaluated on the Embodied Reasoning benchmark and achieved an eighty-seven percent score during testing. This advancement suggests a pathway toward automating complex physical skill acquisition for robotic systems.

items.title: Dream Labs raises $90M and launches Dream API
items.summary: Dream Labs raised $90 million in seed funding and launched the Dream API to translate natural language and camera feeds into robot motor commands. Their Dream-1 model learns how to perform tasks by observing video, allowing it to control new robots without prior specific data. This capability enables zero-shot learning, meaning robots can perform new tasks quickly across different hardware. The Dream API allows developers to connect any robot with grippers to perform tasks instantly. Dream Labs offers fine-tuning services and a robot playground for broader developer access.

items.title: Former OpenAI science lead launches Warp Science to automate wet labs with robots
items.summary: Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil launched Warp Sciences, an AI startup focused on automating wet lab work for drug discovery. The company trains robots to synthesize and test promising compounds identified by researchers. This initiative aims to reshore the labor-intensive work currently outsourced to China and mitigate geopolitical supply-chain risks. Human chemists will train robots to perform various lab tasks, accelerating drug discovery through 24/7 robotic operation. Warp Sciences has raised $215 million and has an $865 million valuation, led by Lightspeed.

items.summary: Infineon named the Italian startup AdapTronics the winner of its 2026 Startup Challenge focused on humanoid robotics and physical AI. items.title: Generative Bionics to build European ‘physical AI data factory’ for humanoid robots
items.summary: Generative Bionics is creating Europe's largest physical AI training facility for humanoid robots, utilizing AMD computing infrastructure for real-world training and digital twin simulation. The initial 5,000-square-meter facility will be built in Italy and operational by late 2027, as part of a planned three-site network. This factory will allow humanoid robots to generate physical data by performing tasks in replicated industrial environments. Models trained through this process, involving simulations of various conditions, are then validated on physical robots in a continuous "real-to-sim-to-real" cycle. The project aims to advance European AI and industrial sovereignty by developing this infrastructure across the continent.

items.title: Just because Tesla’s Optimus is in production doesn’t mean it’s actually ready
items.summary: Tesla is in the process of manufacturing humanoid robots like Optimus while simultaneously working to ensure they are useful, reliable, and durable. CEO Elon Musk acknowledged that significant work remains on the robot's hands, safety, reliability, durability, and the necessary artificial intelligence. Musk anticipates that full delivery to outside companies will occur around the end of 2027, pending the resolution of these challenges. To achieve this, Tesla needs to build a large fleet of robots to generate training data through self-play. Experts suggest that solving the challenges of dexterity and reliability may take longer than Musk's timeline.

items.title: Opinion: Send the robot, not the person. What inspection robots are really for
items.summary: The author developed inspection robots like Spot to allow engineers to gather data from hazardous power substations remotely, thereby reducing human exposure to danger. Robots are intended to collect evidence, but they do not replace the engineer's need to interpret findings and make final decisions. An accurate reading does not always provide sufficient context, meaning physical investigation may still be necessary to fully understand the situation. Therefore, the focus should be on using robots to provide information while retaining human expertise for judgment and necessary on-site actions. The ultimate goal is to enhance safety by outsourcing hazardous tasks while keeping skilled human oversight central to the process.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Opinion: Send the robot, not the person. What inspection robots are really for". This report examines the role of inspection robots in industrial environments and their application in safety protocols. Engineers utilize these robotic systems to gather data from hazardous locations, such as power substations, thereby minimizing direct human exposure to danger. The methodology involves deploying autonomous robots to collect visual and sensor data from areas deemed too dangerous for personnel. These robots are designed to collect evidence, yet the findings necessitate interpretation by human engineers who retain the capacity to contextualize the data and make final decisions. Physical investigation remains necessary to fully understand complex site conditions, emphasizing that robotic data serves to augment, not entirely replace, human expertise in judgment and action. The focus remains on outsourcing hazardous tasks while maintaining human oversight central to the operational process. This trend indicates a continued focus on symbiotic human-machine systems in high-risk industrial applications.

items.title: ETH scientists set to bring Terminator-style robots to life with lab-grown muscles
items.summary: Scientists at ETH created bioactuators by integrating living muscle tissue from mouse cells with 3D-printed hydrogel scaffolds. They designed the muscle and scaffold as a single system using computer simulations to maximize movement. This approach resulted in actuators with visible movement, capable of jumping and moving across surfaces. The successful design highlights the importance of the interaction between living tissue and soft artificial structures. Future challenges include developing long-term nutrient supply and managing the variability of living tissue.

items.title: Warehouse PPE and Hi Vis in the Age of Automation: Keeping People Safe Around the Machines
items.summary: Automation in warehouses necessitates specific Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for personnel sharing space with machinery. While no single legal checklist exists, essential items like high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and gloves are standard practice based on risk assessments. Visibility is crucial as it helps drivers and sensors perceive people, especially in challenging conditions like low light or cold storage. High-visibility clothing must be selected based on the specific role and risk zone, adhering to standards like EN ISO 20471. A comprehensive PPE strategy must also include footwear, hand protection, and proper garment maintenance for optimal safety.

items.title: 120ft emerges from stealth with €576,000 to build humanoid-powered microfactories
items.summary: Swedish robotics startup 120ft raised €576,000 in angel funding to develop autonomous microfactories using humanoid robots for local manufacturing. The company creates modular factories to allow consumer brands to assemble products locally in smaller batches, bypassing long international supply chains. Their system integrates humanoid robots, AI, virtual simulation, and orchestration software to convert designs into digital assembly instructions. 120ft has significantly reduced robot skill training time, aiming for just seven minutes for full assembly by 2027. The funding will support the development of their factory infrastructure and software as they move toward commercial production and future repair services.

items.title: Ep#112: SlipSense and Touch2Trace
items.summary: SlipSense uses a multimodal tactile sensor, the TacV5, combining a piezoresistive array and an accelerometer to detect object slipping with high accuracy. The system detects slip events within 23.1 milliseconds, achieving a 96.7% Macro F1 score on a large dataset of 1.4 million frames. The framework utilizes modality-specific encoders and cross-attention to fuse the spatial pressure and vibration cues, demonstrating that the two modalities are crucially complementary. This system achieves zero-shot transfer to new robotic platforms without retraining, showcasing strong generalization. Touch2Trace further applies tactile feedback to dexterous cable tracing, showing that this tactile input significantly improves performance over proprioception-only methods.
items.audio_script: From RoboPapers, "Ep#112: SlipSense and Touch2Trace" reports on advancements in tactile sensing for robotic applications, with key findings demonstrated through the SlipSense and Touch2Trace systems. The SlipSense system employs a multimodal tactile sensor, the TacV5, integrating a piezoresistive array and an accelerometer to accurately detect object slipping with a detection time of 23.1 milliseconds and a ninety-six point seven percent Macro F1 score across one million frames. The framework utilizes modality-specific encoders and cross-attention to fuse spatial pressure and vibration cues, indicating that these two modalities are complementary for slip detection. Furthermore, the system exhibits zero-shot transfer to novel robotic platforms without retraining, and Touch2Trace shows that tactile feedback significantly enhances dexterous cable tracing compared to proprioception-only methods. These developments suggest increased capability for robust, real-time tactile perception in robotic systems.

items.title: The Sequence Robotics - Issue #957: Generalist and the Rise of Promptable Robots
items.summary: Generalist hypothesizes that large-scale physical pretraining creates a reusable foundation for robot behavior. The method involves short demonstrations to teach new tasks instead of requiring bespoke datasets. Models across GEN-0, GEN-1, and GEN-1.5 have achieved nearly 99% success on selected tasks via in-context physical prompting. The core question remains whether these performance gains translate to successful, long-horizon real-world deployments. The work focuses on enabling robots to perform complex physical interactions through conversational learning.

items.title: TerraTransfer++: Demonstration-Free End-to-End Planner
items.summary: The TerraTransfer++ method proposes a demonstration-free, end-to-end planning approach for autonomous driving. It leverages self-play in vectorized simulators to generate a diverse distribution of driving scenarios without relying on expert demonstrations. A flow-matching trajectory teacher is distilled from this self-play data to guide the planning process. Lightweight adapters are trained to reproduce the teacher's latent space using specific loss functions. This method yields superior closed-loop policies and planners compared to imitation-based methods on relevant benchmarks.

items.title: MPBRS: Multi-Potential-Based Reward Shaping for Unified Reward Configuration in Humanoid Locomotion
items.summary: Designing effective reward functions for humanoid locomotion in reinforcement learning is challenging due to issues with naive reward shaping. Multi-Potential-Based Reward Shaping (MPBRS) is proposed to address this by shaping rewards using potential function differences to guide exploration without altering the optimal policy. The study implements MPBRS for humanoid locomotion and demonstrates a unified reward configuration across nine different robots. Experiments show that MPBRS yields more consistent scaling and reduced sensitivity to tuning compared to standard reward shaping. This makes tuning reward functions simpler across various humanoid robots.

items.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
items.summary: Tactile sensing is crucial for dexterous robotic manipulation by providing direct access to physical contact. Research in this area has evolved from mechanics-driven methods, which interpret signals through contact mechanics, to data-driven approaches learning from tactile data. The paper reviews the fundamentals of tactile sensing and the progression from mechanics-driven to data-driven manipulation. Data-driven methods include imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and vision-language-action models for tactile control. Open challenges remain in achieving scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.

items.title: Integrated Respiratory Sensing and Gated Control for Autonomous Needle Insertion Via CT Bore Robotic Arm
items.summary: A sensing and control system was developed for autonomous needle insertion within a CT bore robotic arm. This system integrates respiratory sensing to achieve gated needle insertion, eliminating the need for manual patient breath-holding. Experiments confirmed the system's capability to track and predict patient breath cycles and detect anomalies. The goal is to automate CT-guided lung biopsy to reduce procedure time and patient discomfort. This approach aims to decrease radiation exposure during the medical procedure.

items.title: Decision Making and Ride Comfort Evaluation Based on Lane-Change Prediction for Autonomous Vehicles
items.summary: Predicting lane-change intentions allows autonomous vehicles to make proactive decisions instead of reactive ones. The study evaluates three driving strategies—reactive, prediction-based longitudinal action, and prediction-based lateral action—in simulated merging scenarios. Prediction-based strategies successfully avoided collisions, reducing peak deceleration before impact by 31.5% and 91.0% compared to reactive driving. Ride comfort is assessed using ISO 2631-1-based horizontal vibration estimates. Overall, lane-change prediction supports safer, smoother driving by enabling proactive decision-making and ride comfort evaluation.
